title: Mixed practice: you drive
idea: REVIEW-HEAVY GUIDED PROBLEM. The learner runs the full UEPCC rhythm on a small report with less scaffolding, mixing earlier Unit 1 print skills with this unit's multi-line ordering.
problem: Show a mini profile card on three lines: a name (Sam), a city (Hue), and a number — their lucky number 7.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: Show name Sam, city Hue, lucky number 7 — one per line.

What is the OUTPUT?
exercises.explanation: Three facts, three lines. You lead this one — start by naming the output.

exercises.prompt: The lucky number 7 — do we print it as text in quotes or as a bare number?
options: Either works — print("7") and print(7) both show 7
Only if we add it to something
exercises.explanation: From Unit 1: both a bare number and a number in quotes print as 7. Either is fine here.

exercises.prompt: Example. Order the output by hand (name, city, number).
exercises.explanation: Sam, Hue, 7. This is the output you will check against.

options: Three print lines, one per fact, in order
exercises.explanation: One print per fact, three facts, in the listed order. You chose the plan yourself.

exercises.prompt: Code. Arrange the three lines (name, city, number).
exercises.explanation: Sam, Hue, 7 — names in quotes, the number bare, in the planned order.

exercises.prompt: Build the city line (it should show Hue).
exercises.explanation: print("Hue") shows the city on its own line.

exercises.prompt:
Check. Output:

Sam
Hue
7

Matches your example?
exercises.explanation: All three facts in the planned order. Check passes — you drove the whole UEPCC rhythm!

exercises.prompt: New card: name Lee, city Oslo, lucky number 9. Same plan — the last line shows?
exercises.explanation: Same shape, new facts. The number is last, so the last line shows 9. The plan generalizes.

exercises.prompt: Review of the whole unit: to report several facts, you use several print lines, and the order you write them is the order shown.
exercises.explanation: That is the heart of Unit 3. Several prints, chosen order — a tidy little report.

exercises.prompt: You can now solve which kind of problem on your own?
options: Report a few known facts as neatly ordered output
exercises.explanation: You finished Unit 3! You can take a few facts and report them in order with print lines. Next up: working an example by hand before you code.
